question: Should exec denylist policy remain unioned across both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json, or should one persisted surface be canonical?
rationale: Both are new public configuration contracts with different owners and editing paths; implementation correctness cannot decide the permanent product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Choose one canonical surface
options.body: Keep the denylist in the exec-approvals policy owner and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface.

options.title: Keep both unioned
options.body: Accept deny-anywhere precedence across both files and explicitly document their ownership, editing, and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Choose one canonical surface
recommendation.body: Keep the denylist in the exec-approvals policy owner and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history-backed owner and authored the adjacent revocation-race work that defines this authorization boundary.
